title: WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) Compatibility Declaration
description: WooCommerce 8.0+ uses High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS/Custom Order Tables) by default. Any extension interacting with orders must declare explicit compatibility using \Automattic\WooCommerce\Utilities\FeaturesUtil during the 'before_woocommerce_init' action hook.
rules: Declare custom_order_tables compatibility using FeaturesUtil::declare_compatibility( 'custom_order_tables', __FILE__, true ).
Never interact directly with wp_posts or wp_postmeta to read or write WooCommerce order records.
anti_patterns: Declaring HPOS compatibility on 'init' or 'plugins_loaded' (too late; WooCommerce will flag extension as incompatible).
Omitting the class_exists check (causes fatal errors on non-WooCommerce installations).
Hardcoding direct SQL queries targeting wp_posts table for order queries.

patterns.name: Declare HPOS Compatibility
patterns.description: Proper declaration of Custom Order Tables compatibility in main plugin file.

title: WooCommerce Order CRUD Operations and Metadata Access
description: With HPOS, order data is stored in dedicated custom tables (wc_orders, wc_orders_meta). All order reads and modifications must use WC_Order getters, setters, and meta methods rather than WordPress core postmeta functions.
rules: Fetch orders using wc_get_order( $order_id ) which returns WC_Order or false.
Write order metadata with $order->update_meta_data( '_terso_affiliate_id', $affiliate_id ) and commit with $order->save().
Hook into order status transitions using 'woocommerce_order_status_completed' or 'woocommerce_order_status_changed'.
anti_patterns: Using get_post_meta( $order_id, '_affiliate_id', true ) (returns empty on HPOS-enabled stores).
Modifying post_status in wp_posts to change order status.

patterns.name: Order Attribution Hook and Meta Persistence
patterns.description: Safely reading and updating order metadata during checkout creation.
